title: Post-Ultra Downtime: How Much is Enough? (iRunFar, 2023-10-03)
population: Coach guidance on time off after an ultramarathon
findings: The one-day-off-per-mile-raced formula is described as a common, conservative rule that does not seem to apply to ultrarunning.

For runners familiar with running with fatigue and soreness, 'easy running the days after an ultra is permissible'; newer runners are advised to take up to a week or three off before returning to some easy running.
'If you are looking forward to running the day after your ultra, do it.' For runners not in the mood to run, 'two to three weeks should do the trick'.
'Running with pain is not normal': see a professional if pain is present and cross-train while it heals.
limitations: One coach's opinion with an 'it depends' answer; no numbers by distance.
implications: Shows the spread in convention: easy running the next day for experienced ultrarunners through up to three weeks off for newcomers, so a single fixed schedule needs an experience or history input.
Pain gate: any injury-type pain should extend the hold regardless of the schedule.

verification.notes: Re-fetched the page twice (WebFetch): Ian Torrence, October 3, 2023; formula, experienced vs newer runners, 'looking forward to running', two to three weeks, and pain quotes confirmed. The 'few take 3+ months off' point is only a rhetorical question on the page and is not used. Practice source (programme, coaching or clinical page): a published convention, not evidence; grade D.
